chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Variety shows versus vaudeville
summary: Green explains that variety shows had chorus girls and production numbers while vaudeville had only headline acts and was more expensive.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, what exactly is the difference between vaudeville and variety shows?

Well, the difference is that variety shows are -- well, they had acts, but they also would have chorus girls, you know, and production numbers going on in a variety show. Where in vaudeville they only had acts.
So basically the production value of variety shows was much more expensive, much greater.

Um-Umm. Vaudeville was more expensive, because each act considered themselves like box office, you know, headliners, stars, see. Sometimes it worked out that way, see. Will Rogers, he was in vaudeville a lot, and Walter Huston, and there was Will Mahoney, danced on a xylophone and so forth. Pat Rooney and people like that.
So you're saying that actually variety shows, even though they had greater production value, in terms of the amount of people, they were less expensive.
Because vaudeville had all top billing.
Names. And variety shows didn't necessarily.
It might have had one top name and the rest were fill-ins in a certain way.
Buck and Bubbles were headliners, I take it.
